clusters.name: Your father Russell and stepmother Bettina's separation, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time your stepparents separated over starting a family, in 1987: your distance from your stepfather deepened, your pull toward your dad strengthened, and you picked for the city chess squad but felt out of your depth. The separation itself opened the period, and by autumn when you made the squad the shifts had piled up.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within the following three years: your late nights worsened, your mother filled in your college forms while you underfunctioned, you fused hard with your closest friend Rafe then clashed with him once a wrist injury stopped your playing, you withdrew into fixing radios and felt lost and low as your mother remarried in the autumn of 1992, your grandmother Lorna was treated for thyroid cancer around the same time, and your father's uncle Clifford came back into the family in 1989 just before. By early 1994 when you found your drive again through an exchange and raced through your degree, the worst had passed, though your anxiety about your father's notice stayed high.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around your relationship with Joelle beginning in 1998 and ending in mid-1999: insomnia began getting in your way before performances though you played the best you ever had and were winning competitions, then you separated and started with a therapist afterward. Two shifts that count sit beside these relationship events, and no one else's shifts show in these months.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within the following two years: you ran out of steam for performing and became less content by the month, you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and were done with performing, you grew distant from your parents and friends, you left Thornbury and moved through Gull Harbour to Fenwick with a partner you met at a winter party, then separated within months and sank into a deep depression once back in Thornbury that winter, you could not face your family while relying on friends, and your grandmother died in February 2004. When you began swimming and requested help from your parents with therapy costs, the family's reactions began to settle.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you were too drained for conversation with your mother and kept distance from her; she pressed to visit you at Alder Creek that July and you kept the door shut on her, then stopped speaking to her when you moved to nursing school that August. Your grandfather Clifford's death around the same time deepened the period. The silence held through your first year at nursing school.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within the following years: you saw your mother a bit less once she came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2017; your sister Tara and her husband James wed and she moved for her airline work; your aunt Imogen's memory was slipping and she began lashing out when muddled, then was started on tests; your cousin Bella had been treated for melanoma years earlier; Wren's brother Leo and his family moved back nearby in 2019; by October 2019 you were constantly feeling you ought to drive projects forward though your job had steadied, you started a sleeping pill, and around Wren's mother's retirement party at the lake that same month Wren became swamped with one thing after another while you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, her family talked all day with nothing happening to one that the others didn't hear, and you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, feeling you didn't belong.
